entries.topic: Muscadet: Melon alone only in the three named zones
entries.claim: The Loire record calls Melon de Bourgogne Muscadet's only grape and says Muscadet is Melon de Bourgogne alone, and the Régionale question i-r0p7056l says Melon has been the sole grape of Muscadet ever since the winter of 1709.
entries.finding: The specification of the plain Muscadet AOC names Melon B as principal grape and Chardonnay B as an accessory grape, at no more than 10 per cent of a holding's plantings. INAO's standing committee took up the change in 2017, it went to national opposition in November 2018, it stands in the specification homologated by the arrêté of 5 February 2021 (amended 27 May 2021), and the arrêté of 26 November 2025 (JORF of 3 December 2025) keeps it. Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, Muscadet Coteaux de la Loire and Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu remain Melon B alone. The history in the question stands: the specification's link to origin says the hard winter of 1709 destroyed most of the Nantes vineyard and Melon, which bears frost better, was replanted, and InterLoire says the same.

targets.old: Muscadet's only grape: neutral, bone dry
targets.new: Muscadet's grape, alone in Sèvre et Maine and the two smaller zones: neutral, bone dry

targets.old: Muscadet is Melon de Bourgogne alone, a neutral, acid grape brought from Burgundy.
targets.new: Muscadet is Melon de Bourgogne, a neutral, acid grape brought from Burgundy, alone in Sèvre et Maine and the two smaller zones; plain Muscadet may add a little Chardonnay.

targets.new: It has been Muscadet's grape ever since, still alone in Sevre et Maine though plain Muscadet now admits a little Chardonnay, and is scarcely grown in Burgundy today.

entries.why: The plain appellation has admitted an accessory Chardonnay since its specification was revised, so only the three named zones are Melon alone; the 1709 story is the rule's own and stays.

entries.claim: The CMS Loire question e-ddtr2ora says the Melon variety came from Burgundy after the hard winter of 1709.
entries.finding: Melon was already in the Pays Nantais before 1709: the Muscadet specification puts the first written traces of plantings under the name Muscadet in the middle of the seventeenth century (a lease of 1635 kept at Gorges), and after the winter of 1709 Melon was replanted across the vineyard. The frost made it the grape of the region; it did not bring it.

targets.old: the variety came from Burgundy after the hard winter of 1709.
targets.new: the variety came from Burgundy and took over the Pays Nantais after the hard winter of 1709.

sources.title: INAO, cahier des charges de l'AOC Muscadet, procédure nationale d'opposition of November 2018
sources.says: The first written traces of plantings under the name Muscadet date from the middle of the seventeenth century; after the hard winter of 1709 Melon, more resistant to frost, was replanted.

sources.title: InterLoire, Vins de Loire: Melon B
sources.says: Melon was planted massively after the frost of 1709.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Muscadet
sources.says: The name Muscadet first appears in 1635 in a lease at Gorges; Melon became dominant after the frost of 1709 killed most of the vines.

entries.why: The frost of 1709 spread the grape across the Pays Nantais; the grape itself was there before it, so the explanation should not date its arrival to 1709.

entries.claim: The Burgundy record says Bouzeron, the one village appellation for Aligoté, was created in 1997, in its places note and in question r-rkgv0zwg.
entries.finding: INAO's specification for Bouzeron says the appellation was initially recognised by the decree of 17 February 1998, replacing the regional Bourgogne Aligoté Bouzeron of 1979, and the WIPO Lisbon register of 1998 cites the same decree. The 1997 date in many trade pages is the first vintage sold under the village name; one wiki names an INAO decision of 24 September 1997 that no primary text read here confirms.

targets.old: The one village appellation for Aligoté, created in 1997.
targets.new: The one village appellation for Aligoté, decreed in 1998, with 1997 as its first vintage.

targets.old: became a village appellation for Aligoté in 1997;
targets.new: became a village appellation for Aligoté by a decree of February 1998, with 1997 as its first vintage;
